texts.preamble: Firm Basant Bakery, Jiwajiganj Lashkar ... vs State Of M.P. on 4 November, 2015 Mcrc. 1323/2012 1 High Court Of Madhya Pradesh Bench At Gwalior Justice Sujoy Paul. Misc. Criminal Case No. 1323/2012 Firm Basant Bakery and others Vs. State of Mp -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Order
texts.facts: This petition filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) challenges the order dated 13.7.2010, whereby the Judicial Magistrate First Class (JMFC) Gwalior in Criminal Case No. 579/2008 has taken cognizance and charges were directed to be framed against the petitioners. The Revisional Court's order passed in CR No.394/2010 dated 26.9.2011 is also called in question in this petition. The samples of biscuits were taken on 30.3.2000 by the Food Inspector. As per the date of manufacturing mentioned in the packet of biscuits (March 2000), its expiry period was within five months from the date of manufacturing the biscuits. Thus, the expiry date of biscuits was up to July, 2000, whereas the complaint was filed on 7.8.2000. As per Section 13 (2) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (for short, the "PFA Act"), no fruitful purpose would be served to send the biscuits to Central Food Laboratory for analysis. Hence, the petitioners have been deprived from their valuable right by not filing the complaint before the expiry date of biscuits, which caused prejudice to the petitioners.
texts.arguments: 2. Shri R.K.Sharma, learned counsel for the petitioners, submits that the complaint was filed against the petitioners on 2.7.2000. In support of aforesaid contention, h relied on AIR 1994 SC 1818 (T.V.Usman v. Food Inspector, Tellicherry Municipality, Tellicherry). Lastly, he relied on the statement of Shri N.R.Jatav, who was Food Inspector at the relevant time. On the basis of para 13 of said statement, Shri Sharma contended that the date of manufacturing mentioned in the packet of biscuits should be treated as 1.3.2000. Thus after expiry of period, no fruitful purpose would be served to permit the prosecution to continue because the petitioners' right flowing from Section 13(2) of PFA Act is taken away. 3. Shri Kamal Jain, learned Government Advocate, on the other hand, opposed the relief. He submitted that the revisional court has considered the contentions of the petitioners. Hence, no interference be made. Even otherwise, he contents that no case is made out for interference under Firm Basant Bakery, Jiwajiganj Lashkar ... vs State Of M.P. on 4 November, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161442867/ 1 Article 482 CrPC. 4. 6. In (2012) 9 SCC 460 (Amit Kapoor vs. Ramesh Chander). The Apex Court has culled out following basic principles on which jurisdiction under Section 397/482 CrPC can be exercised:- 1. Though there are no limits of the powers of the Court under Section 482 CrPC but the more the power, the more due care and caution is to be exercised in invoking these powers. The power of quashing criminal proceedings, particularly, the charge framed in terms of Section 228 CrPC should be exercised very sparingly and with circumspection and that too in the rarest of rare cases. If the allegations are so patently absurd and inherently improbable that no prudent person can ever reach such a conclusion and where the basic ingredients of a criminal offence are not satisfied then the Court may interfere. Firm Basant Bakery, Jiwajiganj Lashkar ... vs State Of M.P. on 4 November, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161442867/ 2 8.
